chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with buying green crops, then leaving them until you harvest them if you wish, or feeding them [to animals] before they form ears, while they are still grass.
And he (peace be upon him) said: There is also no problem with buying crops that have already formed ears and ripened with wheat.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy green crops before harvest in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of trading green crops (sabaq) by clarifying that the seller retains the right to either harvest the crop or graze it as fodder before full maturity, provided the specific state of the crop is known. It further validates the sale of crops that have already formed ears and ripened, reflecting the practical agricultural norms of early Shia jurisprudence where uncertainty (gharar) was minimized by clear physical identification of the asset.
